title: Help Comes at the Right Time

text: The trouble came near sunset.
The older man was driving home when the car began to shake.
The quiet felt too quiet.
He sat for a moment with both hands on the wheel.
He was not lost, but he was far enough from town to feel alone.
The road had fields on one side and trees on the other.
The last of the light was slipping away.
"Lord," he said quietly, "I could use some help.".
The air cooled as the sun dropped behind the trees.
A few cars passed, but none slowed.
He locked the doors and waited.
The first car that stopped did not feel right.
Two men got out and walked toward him too slowly.
The voice did not sound like help.
The older man had lived long enough to hear what words did not say.
These men were not in a hurry to fix the car.
They were studying him, his hands, his age, and whether anyone else was nearby.
"I have someone coming," he said.
Not yet.
The man reached for the door handle.
The older man hit the horn and held it down.
And sometimes noise is a wall.
Then headlights came around the bend.
Not far off.
Help had not come early, but it had come on time.
The older man kept the horn pressed until the truck pulled in behind the stopped car.
It was a county service truck, dusty.
Ordinary, with a yellow light on top.
A man in a work jacket stepping out.
"Good thing I came this way," he said.
The older man nodded.
He could have said it was luck.
That mattered.
Later, the older man sat in the tow truck.
Looked back at the road.
He was tired, but he was thankful.
He thought about how close that time had felt.
A quiet road.
A dead car.
Two men who had not come to help.
And it had come at the right time.
When he got home, he sat for a while before going inside.
He thanked God quietly, not with fancy words.
Help came around the bend, and mercy had headlights.
